focus: 안 되다 (an doeda) = 'it doesn't work / won't do' – the broad complaint use of 되다; fix the em dash and the '-essential' zinger.
잘못 + verb = 'do it wrong' pattern (잘못 봤어요 = misread); romanize the example chunk, not just 잘못.
쯤 suffixes onto the quantity itself to mean 'about' (세 시간쯤 = about three hours); romanize the full example chunk.
-보다 = 'than' attaches to the noun being compared against (편도보다 = than one-way); cut the double vocab gloss, romanize 보다.
가르치다 means both 'teach' and 'tell/show the way' (길을 가르쳐 줬어요); add romanization, drop the em dash.
놓고 오다 = 'put it down and came' – Korean narrates leaving something behind as two actions; dup-group of 2, dedup against the sibling and fix the em dash.
Memories arise on their own in Korean – 추억이 생기다, not 'make' memories; cut the gloss lead, romanize 생겼어요.
Korean has native words for day-counts – 하루 (one day), 이틀 (two days) – instead of number + 'day'; fix parens to (romanization = gloss) format and the em dash.
-어 보세요 softens a command into 'give it a try' (가 보세요 = try going); cut the tacked-on 꼭 second rule.
쓰다 covers both 'write' and 'use' (써 보세요 = try using it); fix the em dash.
-부터 = 'starting with', including priorities not just times (여권부터 = passport first); romanize the example chunk.
하고 = 'and' only between nouns (수영복하고 모자); romanize the example chunk.
Plans are 'stood up' in Korean – 계획을 세우다 literally 'stand a plan'; fix the em dash.
붙다 literally 'stick' – passing an exam/screening is sticking to it (서류 전형에 붙었어요); lead with the literal logic, not the gloss.
떨어지다 literally 'fall' – failing is falling off (서류에서 떨어졌어요), the mirror of 붙다 'stick' = pass.
Current tip just re-glosses 때문에; pivot to the doctrine exemplar insight – 긴장돼요 uses 되다 'become': nerves happen to you in Korean, not something you are.
-아/어 주다 marks doing something FOR someone (설명해 주셨어요 = explained for me); keep to that one rule and romanize every cited chunk.
Subjects you honor take -(으)시- inside the verb (부장님이 시작하셨어요); romanize 부장님이 too.
-들 marks plural (동료들) and Korean often leaves it off; cut the vocab-gloss lead, romanize the plural form.
께 replaces 한테 when the receiver outranks you (부장님께); romanize 한테 as well.
여쭤보다 = the humble 'ask' for superiors, vs plain 물어보다; romanize 께 in this tip.
-이나 after a quantity adds 'a whole / as much as' (세 시간이나) – matches the card's surprise; cut to that one rule and romanize it.
도움이 되다 literally 'become a help' – helpful things 'become' in Korean (도움이 됐어요); romanize the past form.
살리다 = 'bring to life', also 'put to use' for skills/experience (경력을 살려서); drop the bolted-on -(으)ㄹ 거예요 second rule.
Other people's feelings take -어하다 (아쉬워하셨어요) – you can't state someone else's inner state bare; romanize every cited chunk.
좋다 states your own feeling; others' liking needs 좋아하다 (좋아하셨어요); romanize 좋다 too.
Adjectives also take -(으)세요 for an honored subject (좋으세요 describing 팀장님); romanize 팀장님.
-는 거예요 turns a verb into 'the act of doing' so it can follow 'my goal is...' (되는 거예요); the current 'it is (doing)' gloss is opaque.
-아/어도 괜찮아요 = 'it's okay even if' (실수해도); romanize 괜찮아요.
Adjectives need -(으)ㄴ before a noun: 새로운 일 = new work; frame as the before-a-noun rule, not a form-derivation arrow, and romanize 새로운 일.
-는 게 turns a verb into a 'doing' noun you can like/dislike (일하는 게 좋아요); romanize 좋아요.
더 after a quantity = 'more' (하나 더 = one more) – a better angle than repeating the native-numbers rule already told on ko-2440; romanize 더.
얼마 없다 literally 'there isn't even how-much' = hardly any (잔액이 얼마 없어요); cut the 잔액 gloss lead, romanize the phrase.
긁다 literally 'scratch' – card spending is 'scratching the card' (카드를 긁었어요); lead with the literal logic, romanize the phrase.
